answer: Sequential time-lock puzzles mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring non-parallelizable computation to register an identity. An attacker must expend dedicated processor time, slowing bot deployment to the pace of a glacier. The output provides crystal certainty of elapsed computation, which peers verify as swiftly as a falcon. A key limitation is that adversaries with custom ASIC hardware evaluate sequential cycles faster than standard systems, reducing their marginal registration expense.
